description.narrative: Sarus Exchange Program aims to dispel stereotypes and build mutual understanding between future leaders from bordering nations with a history of conflict. Taking this successful model Sarus inaugurated Bangladesh-Myanmar Exchange Program, held from June through August 2016, focusing on young women leaders from these two bordering nations. The target population for this program is young women in both countries, as women are not only disproportionately affected and made vulnerable by conflict, but also face great challenges in gender equality and access to opportunities. Moreover, the perpetuation of harmful gender-based stereotypes in Myanmar makes women’s role as social actors in the public sector extremely difficult. The Bangladesh- Myanmar Exchange Program will bring together 12 young women leaders for six weeks for an experiential learning through shared living in both countries, conflict transformation, gender empowerment, and community development workshops, and collaborative service projects with local peacebuilding organizations. After participants return home, the program will continue for an additional three and a half months through their own community service projects that they design, implement, and evaluate with support from Sarus staff.
